other_findings.message: Sponsor sub-process entered by two message types through one start event: accepted by the orchestrator as one business trigger ('Intentional protocol deviation communicated'), with the deciding task A14 before G1 (conflicts.md C-27, rule_exceptions FLW-09, revisitable by the user). No repair needed.

New deciding task 'Review intentional protocol deviation communication' (Sponsor lane) carries only investigator REQs - REQ-073 (21CFR312.53(c)(1)(vi)(a): the investigator notifies the sponsor before changes), REQ-080 (E6R3 A1-2.5.4: the investigator informs the sponsor) and REQ-074 (FDA-PD24 draft: the investigator obtains prior sponsor approval) - so a sponsor step that no source names (its own [verify] item says so) shows LAW. The same REQs already sit on the investigator tasks A10, A12 and on M1, M3. Repair: give A14 a sponsor-side REQ (e.g. REQ-076 'consider each investigator request', FDA-PD24 draft, and the receipt side of REQ-083) or mark its binding as derived from the incoming messages, so the badge does not claim a binding sponsor obligation.

SCP-02: one trigger and named outcomes per sub-process; L4-05 E2 renamed 'No notification required' (true on every path, l3_cut aligned); L4-03 S1 accepted exception (C-27)

LBL-04: no bare 'CSR' left (L4-07 uses 'clinical study report'), no 'important deviation' / 'intentional deviation' short forms, L4-08 tasks use the EU CTR term 'clinical trial master file' and the data stores the E6R3 terms 'Trial master file' / 'Investigator site file' (both glossary terms); no 'protocol violation', no bare 'CTR'
